dream.title: Memory Dream
dream.description: Nightly, Dream looks for exact duplicates, expired notes, and near-duplicate clusters in your memory. It archives the redundant ones (never deletes) so the surviving notes stay clean and useful.

status.noRunYet: No cycle has run yet on this machine.
status.catchupHint: Missed nights catch up on the next Isoform launch — no cycle is silently skipped.

settings.enabledHelp: When on, Dream runs at the scheduled time each day. When off, you can still trigger it manually.
settings.dailyTimeHelp: Local time. 03:00 is the default so the cycle doesn't compete with active use. If Isoform isn't running at this time, Dream catches up the next time you open Isoform that day — so you never lose a cycle.
settings.dryRunOnlyHelp: Strongly recommended for the first two weeks. Scheduled runs produce a preview report instead of archiving anything. You commit a preview from the Overview tab.
settings.llmEnabledHelp: Layer 3 lets Haiku decide what to merge for clusters in the borderline similarity band. Costs tokens. Turn off to skip and run only the rule-based + tight-similarity layers.
settings.similarityThresholdHelp: Cosine similarity at or above this is auto-merged without an LLM. Default 0.95 — strict on purpose; near-duplicates that share most but not all content stay safe.
settings.llmMergeLowHelp: Pairs in [this, auto-merge] go to Haiku for review. Default 0.80.
settings.llmBatchSizeHelp: Max memories sent to Haiku in one call. Bigger batches are cheaper per merge but slower per call. Default 8.
settings.archiveRetentionDaysHelp: Archived memories older than this are permanently deleted. Default 30.
settings.advancedHint: Don't change these unless you understand cosine similarity over text embeddings.

safety.title: How Dream protects your memories
items: Dream archives memories instead of permanently deleting them. Removed entries move to memory/.archive/ as markdown files you can restore.
Memories you've manually edited (with version history) always win as survivor — Dream will never demote them.
Memories from different dimensions are never auto-merged across dimensions.

Every deletion is gated by a single-survivor coverage check: some specific surviving memory (kept or synthesized) must contain at least 85% of the deleted memory's distinct facts. This catches the symmetric-overlap case where two memories share most content but each carries a unique fact that would otherwise quietly disappear.
The vector-only fast path (cosine >= 0.95) is no longer trusted blindly — it runs the same coverage check, and on failure the cluster is demoted to Haiku review instead of auto-merging.
Clusters larger than 20 entries are skipped entirely (anti-hub defense) — they're usually transitive chains through a generic concept, not real redundancy.
Every cycle is reversible by run ID for 30 days.
